cases.why: the Wilson interval drops its z-squared term and becomes the normal approximation, wrong exactly in the small tail bins this module exists for.
a bin with no games reports an interval of exactly zero, a certainty measured from nothing.
a probability of exactly 1.0 falls out of every bin, so the bins stop accounting for every game.

cases.why: a bin of a handful of games is drawn like a measured one, the failure the underpowered flag exists to prevent.
resolution is measured from each bin's own forecast instead of the base rate, so a model that always says the base rate looks informative.
reliability sums absolute gaps, so the Murphy identity Brier = reliability - resolution + uncertainty no longer holds.
every bin is marked consistent with perfect calibration, whatever its interval says.
